title: Placement tests
summary: Who tests, how to send and proctor the test, and where the score report goes.

la: Proctor placement tests and send the score report
lc: Recommend a placement; set up oral interviews

nodes.text: Save the report as PDF, email it

sections.title: Who takes the test
list: **1002**: no test. There's no prerequisite, so the student just registers.
**2001 and higher**: the test is required.
**Cumming, Blue Ridge or online students**: remote testing only if the coordinator approves it. Everyone else tests in the Lab.
sections.note: Answering a placement email? Start with the [first reply](#/replies/placement-intake). The Lab never advises on courses: that's the student's advisor or the department.

sections.title: Seat the student
steps: Student sits at a Lab computer, opens Chrome and their UNG email.
Check the student's name and UNG email; that's where the test is sent. Don't write them down anywhere else.

sections.title: Send the test (Emmersion)
steps: Log in to Emmersion with your campus Lab account. Passwords are on the internal quick reference sheet, never in an email.
**Send Assessments** > **Get Started** under Send via Email.
Enter the student's UNG email (commas between several), **Continue**.
Open **Assessments**, pick the language (Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, Russian, Spanish), **Continue**.
The student refreshes their inbox, opens the link and finishes every part.

sections.title: Send the score report
steps: **Dashboard** > Assessment Results > click the student's name.
Click **Show Scale** and open **Survey Details**, so every sub-score shows.
Ctrl + P, Destination **Save as PDF**, tick Background graphics.
From the Lab email, send it to the coordinator: "[Name] finished the [language] placement test."
sections.note: Don't tell the student a course. Placement is the coordinator's call.

sections.title: Coordinator: recommend
list: Read the report (CEFR estimate and score range).
Heritage or native speaker: set up an oral interview with a faculty member.
Email the recommendation, the PDF and the student's details to the department ({dept}) or that language's lead.
Approve or refuse remote testing; handle exceptions and honesty concerns.
